about: Behaviour the .NET and Node hosts share, run by ScriptBox.Tests/ConformanceTests.cs and ScriptBox.Node/test/conformance.test.ts. Each host registers the same 'conf' namespace. Both hosts must meet every expectation; there are no per-host cases.

methods.echo: echo(value: any): any. Returns its argument.
methods.greet: greet(name: string, greeting?: string = 'Hello'): string. Returns greeting + ', ' + name.
methods.fail: fail(message: string): never. Throws an API error named ConfError with the message.
methods.record: record(tag: string): void. Appends conf.record:<tag> to the host's call log.
methods.item: item(id: string): { id: string, name: string }. Returns { id, name: 'Item ' + id }.
methods.rename: rename(change: { id: string, name: string }): { id: string, name: string }. Returns the change.
methods.crash: crash(): void. Fails on the host with an internal error whose message must not reach the script.

cases.name: JSON values round-trip through a host call
cases.script: return await conf.echo({ s: 'x', n: 1.5, i: -2, b: true, z: null, a: [1, 'two', [3]], o: { deep: { er: [] } } });

cases.name: positional arguments bind in order
cases.script: return await conf.add(2, 3);

cases.name: an omitted trailing argument takes its default
cases.script: return [await conf.greet('Ada'), await conf.greet('Ada', 'Hi')];

cases.name: a script with no return completes with no value
cases.script: const x = 1;

cases.name: a returned property set to undefined is left out
cases.script: return { a: 1, b: undefined };

cases.name: a void method resolves to nothing
cases.script: const r = await conf.record('v'); return r === undefined ? 'undefined' : r === null ? 'null' : typeof r;

cases.name: an API error is catchable with its name and message
cases.script: try { await conf.fail('not today'); return 'no error'; } catch (e) { return [e.name, e.message]; }

cases.name: an uncaught API error fails the script with its name
cases.script: await conf.fail('not today');

cases.name: a thrown error reports its line in the submitted source
a syntax error reports its line
calls run in the order the script makes them
cases.script: await conf.record('a'); await conf.record('b'); conf.record('c'); return 1;

cases.name: a global set by one execution is gone in the next
cases.script: return [typeof leaked, ({}).polluted === undefined];

cases.name: runtime filters wrap session filters, each in the order added
cases.script: await conf.record('f'); return 1;

cases.name: a filter can answer in the method's place
cases.script: return await conf.item('a');

cases.name: a filter can refuse a call with an error the script can catch
cases.script: try { await conf.add(1, 2); return 'added'; } catch (e) { return [e.name, e.message]; }

cases.name: sealed results refuse new properties and keep arrays growable
cases.script: const i = await conf.item('a'); const list = await conf.echo([1]); list.push(2); i.name = 'changed'; try { i.extra = 1; return 'added'; } catch (e) { return [e.name, i.name, list.length]; }

cases.name: a changed result is the script's copy only
cases.script: const a = await conf.item('a'); a.name = 'changed'; const b = await conf.item('a'); return b.name;

cases.name: the docs list a namespace folder README first, then its files by path
cases.script: return (await docs.ls('/api/conf')).map((e) => e.path);

cases.name: docs.read reports a missing file per path, without failing the batch
cases.script: const files = await docs.read(['/api/conf/README.md', '/api/conf/nope.d.ts']); return files.map((f) => [f.path, f.content === null, f.error === null]);

cases.name: docs.grep finds a method in its declaration files
cases.script: const hits = await docs.grep('greet\\(', '/api/conf'); return [...new Set(hits.map((h) => h.path))].sort();

cases.name: docs paths cannot climb out of the tree
cases.script: const [f] = await docs.read(['/api/../../etc/passwd']); return [f.content === null, f.error !== null];

cases.name: an unknown method fails catchably
cases.script: try { await __scriptbox.hostCall('conf.missing', []); return 'called'; } catch (e) { return e.name; }

cases.name: a value with no JSON form
cases.script: return NaN;

cases.name: a host call returns a promise
cases.script: const p = conf.add(1, 2); return [typeof p.then, await p];

cases.name: a call the script did not await still runs before the outcome
cases.script: conf.record('late'); return 1;

cases.name: a call that fails and that nothing handles fails the execution
cases.script: conf.fail('lost'); return 1;

cases.name: awaiting a promise nothing can settle fails the execution
cases.script: await new Promise(() => {}); return 1;

cases.name: a failed host call points at the line that made it
cases.script:
const a = 1;
await conf.fail('here');

cases.name: an internal host failure reaches the script without its message
cases.script: try { await conf.crash(); return "called"; } catch (e) { return [e.name, e.message]; }

cases.name: an argument with a property its type does not declare is refused
cases.script: try { await conf.rename({ id: 'a', name: 'b', extra: 1 }); return 'called'; } catch (e) { return e.name; }

cases.name: null is a value, not an omitted argument
cases.script: try { return await conf.greet('Ann', null); } catch (e) { return e.name; }

cases.name: calls beyond the outstanding limit are refused before they start
cases.script: const ps = []; for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) ps.push(conf.add(i, 0).then(() => 'ok', (e) => e.name)); const r = await Promise.all(ps); return [r.filter((x) => x === 'ok').length, r.filter((x) => x === 'QueueFullError').length];

cases.name: calls a failed script made in its last step never start
cases.script: conf.record('x'); throw new Error('stop');

cases.name: an omitted argument before a given one is refused when it has no default
cases.script: try { await conf.greet(undefined, 'Hi'); return 'called'; } catch (e) { return e.name; }

cases.name: a filter that gives a void method a value fails the call
cases.script: try { await conf.record('x'); return 'called'; } catch (e) { return [e.name, e.message]; }

value: conf.record returned a value but declares no result.

cases.name: a call made after the script returned is revoked
cases.script: globalThis.r = conf.add(1, 2).then(() => conf.add(3, 4)); return 1;

cases.name: a runtime SyntaxError is a script error, not invalid source
cases.script: JSON.parse('{');
